- `tile_a[1..31][*]` are NEVER written (contain garbage/uninitialized values)
- When reading `tile_a[threadIdx.y][k]` in the dot product, threads with `threadIdx.y > 0` read garbage

Previous attempts failed because:
1. **Uniform values per row** - When all rows have similar values, even race-condition writes produce similar results
2. **Normalization masking** - BatchNorm and GroupNorm normalize the outputs, so even corrupted GEMM values get normalized to similar ranges when the corruption is uniform

## Step 2 — Pivot Strategy

Use **per-row unique sparse patterns** - place non-zero values at different column positions for different rows. This ensures that if thread for row N reads tile_a[garbage] instead of tile_a[N], it gets completely wrong data since different rows contribute to different weight columns.

## Step 3 — Construct Concrete Input

Each row gets a single large non-zero value at a unique column position (within the first tile). This maximizes the difference between correct tile_a[row] data and garbage data in tile_a[row!=0].
